newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Senate panel okays $260 mln hike for schools.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Senate panel okays $260 mln hike for schools.

text.p: The New Jersey Senate Education Committee late Thursday approved a school funding proposal that would increase state aid to schools by $260 million.
The Republican-backed plan also increases by $65 million the amount Gov. Christine Whitman proposed in her own school reform package released earlier this year.
The committee's vote was split 3-2 along party lines.

New Jersey is facing a court-imposed Dec. 31 deadline to equalize spending among rich and poor school districts, the latest stage in a decades-long battle over the meaning of state constitutional requirements for a "thorough and efficient" education.

Sen. Robert Martin, R-Morris Plains, sponsored the bill. He said it would reduce the number of districts that could potentially lose state aid and increase by $15 million property tax relief for middle-class districts.
"We promised that we wouldn't pass a bill that would result in the dumbing down of the level of excellence enjoyed by many of our school district," Martin said.
But Democratic legislative leaders said the plan underestimates spending needs, and would force middle-class districts to rely more heavily on property taxes.

Under the bill, 28 districts singled out by the state Supreme Court as in need of special help would share about $134 million in new state aid. Jersey City is in line for a 17.4 percent rise of $34 million, the largest of the group.
A total of 26 district would lose some of their state aid under the plan, commensurate with enrollment declines. Whitman's plan would have reduced state aid to 125 districts.
The bill next faces a vote in the Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee.
